# BOOM Drinkware

> BOOM Drinkware is a drinkware factory in Shenzhen, China, running injection moulding and silicone compression moulding in house since 2013. The site lists drinkware and barware models with capacity, material and decoration options, and takes custom, private-label and OEM/ODM projects.

Key facts:

- Founded: 2013
- Plant: 3,416 m², Shenzhen
- Equipment: injection moulding, silicone compression moulding and our own tooling shop in house; 65 machines across 4 production lines
- Quality: 4 full-time QA/QC inspectors, AQL sampling (under 500 pcs 5%, 500-2000 pcs 3%, over 2000 pcs 1%)
- Materials: plastic (PP, Tritan, AS, PS) and silicone; metal parts are sourced from vetted suppliers
- Terms: T/T 30% deposit and 70% against copy of B/L, FOB Shenzhen; PayPal for samples only

- [Custom plastic and Tritan cups](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/custom-plastic-cups/)

## Guides

- [How many custom cups should you order?](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/blog/how-many-custom-cups-to-order/): the three minimums behind one MOQ number (per order, per colour, per mould), where 10 / 250 / 1,000 / 3,000 pieces come from, setup-per-piece arithmetic, the break-even quantity formula, spares percentage by event type, how splitting colours multiplies setup, when ordering more costs more
- [Sampling and production lead times](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/blog/custom-cup-lead-times/): day-by-day anatomy of the 7-12 day sample window, sample types compared, where days disappear, the eight production stages behind 25-30 days, Chinese holiday calendar table, sea vs rail vs air transit days, what a delivery date cannot promise
- [Silicone vs plastic cups](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/blog/silicone-vs-plastic-cups/): rigid vs flexible behaviour, spec table (temperature, clarity, weight, wall, entry quantity), print method compatibility on each surface, freight arithmetic for 500 cups by weight and carton volume, ageing behaviour, five recurring buying mistakes
- [Does a custom cup need a new mould?](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/blog/mould-or-no-mould/): the three levels of existing tooling, the arithmetic that decides when a new mould pays for itself, the six factors that move a mould price, cavity-count output table, bridge vs production steel, six stages from drawing to shippable cup
- [Why a cup colour does not match the Pantone chip](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/blog/plastic-colour-matching/): the four rendering stages, Pantone vs Pantone Plastics vs physical sample, what ΔE values mean in practice, masterbatch vs pre-compound, seven process variables that shift colour, colour approval checklist and repeat-order controls
- [What an AQL inspection actually tells you](https://www.boomdrinkware.com/blog/what-aql-inspection-tells-you/): ISO 2859-1 sample-size table for common lot sizes, why a passing lot is not a defect-free lot, AQL levels by defect class, a drinkware defect list with test methods, six things inspection cannot see, how to read a report and what to do when a lot fails
